sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Mandate**: The Commission was tasked with preparing a body of substantive law for India, specifically focusing on areas where English law could be adapted to Indian conditions.
• **Leadership**: Chaired by **Sir John Romilly**, who was the Master of the Rolls in England, ensuring a direct link between British legal expertise and Indian colonial administration.
• **Primary Output**: The Commission was instrumental in drafting the **Indian Succession Act (1865)** and the **Indian Contract Act (1872)**, which form the bedrock of modern Indian civil jurisprudence.
• **Legal Philosophy**: The commission operated on the principle of **'Codification'**, aiming to replace the diverse and often ambiguous personal laws and local customs with a uniform, written legal code.

items.definition: The process of collecting and restating the law of a jurisdiction in certain areas, usually by subject, forming a legal code.
The set of laws that governs how members of a society are to behave, as opposed to procedural law which governs the process of the courts.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Uniformity**: Aimed to reduce the complexity of multiple personal laws by introducing uniform civil codes for specific areas.
• **Legal Infrastructure**: Provided the necessary legal framework to support the growing commercial and administrative needs of the British Empire in India.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Resistance from traditional religious communities regarding interference in personal laws.
• **Solutions**: Gradual implementation and selective application of codes to ensure minimal social friction.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'ROM-CON-SUC'
• **Decoded Meaning**: **ROM**illy (Chairman) led the commission that drafted the **CON**tract Act and the **SUC**cession Act.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the First Law Commission (Macaulay, 1834) with the Third Law Commission (Romilly, 1862). Remember: Macaulay = Penal Code (IPC); Romilly = Succession/Contract Acts.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Legal Imperialism' or 'Codification of Colonial Law' to describe the impact of these commissions on the Indian legal landscape.

keyTakeaways: The Third Law Commission (1862) was chaired by Sir John Romilly.
It was responsible for the drafting of the Indian Succession Act (1865) and the Indian Contract Act (1872).
The commission's primary goal was the codification of substantive law to ensure uniformity across British India.
